Sunday, December 14, 2025, 5:34 PM: More consistency of an aggressive weather pattern developing around Christmas time continues to be exhibited by a series of CPC guidance and illustrated water vapor satellite shows, and an abundance of powerful and dynamic Pacific storms lining up in the southern latitude from the Philippines, and the Marshall Islands. 

This particular situation is what I was watching very closely over the past month as a 1028 mb surface high that was over California continue to warm the pacific from Northern California down to Baja California at about 5 to 8° warmer than average for December averages putting another boost to a strong pacific jet extension that potentially will have significant impacts between December 24 on Christmas Eve to December 28. 

The combination of this particular situation continues to be watched over the next week as this does have a possibility of being very heavy rainfall, not just to Southern California, but also to Northern and Central California as well. 

As you have all seen what has happened in the Pacific Northwest over the past week, there has been significant flooding concerns in Washington state where rivers have reached historical levels were possible flood concerns indicated by the ongoing long duration of the Marshall Islands low axis not just affecting the Pacific Northwest, but also having impact now potentially affecting our region as we wrap up December 2025. #CAwx

GM CT - GM CODEX FAMS !!!

@codexfx: The Next Generation Cross Border Payment Solution

1. The Real Problem: Cost & Speed in International Payments

For example: When you send money from Vietnam to Singapore, Malaysia, or Europe, you are facing major barriers:

- Slow Time: 3-7 days for the money to reach the recipient.

- High Cost: Transfer fees range from 6-7%, potentially amounting to millions of VND for large transactions.

- Poor Exchange Rates: Exchange rate spread of 2-4% compared to the market rate.

- Lack of Transparency: Unaware of where the money is or when it will arrive.

- Liquidity Risk: Funds can be frozen mid-transfer due to compliance issues.

This is the core problem that the traditional banking system has failed to solve for decades.

2. @codexfx Solution

@codexfx is an Ethereum Layer 2 blockchain fully optimized for stablecoins and B2B payments. It launched its mainnet in June 2024 with $15.8M in funding from Dragonfly Capital, Coinbase Ventures, and Circle Ventures.

3 Technology Pillars:
- Ultra-Low Cost: Transaction fees are <0.1 cent, tens of times lower than traditional systems.

- Native Stablecoin Support: Direct support for USDC (native mint/burn), EURC, and TRYB; gas fees paid in stablecoins.

- @codexfx Avenue On-Chain FX Platform: Direct, atomic swaps of currency pairs (USD/EUR/NGN/BRL) at near 1:1 exchange rates, with integrated KYC/AML.

3. Why Is @codexfx Different?

While other blockchains are designed for general purpose (trading, DeFi, NFTs), @codexfx is 100% focused on payments and stablecoins:

- No gas fee volatility due to a fee dampening mechanism stable fees even under network congestion.

- Ethereum Security – every transaction is settled on the Ethereum mainnet.

- Issuer Neutral – supports all stablecoins, non proprietary.

- Enterprise API – easy integration for fintechs, banks, and multinational corporations.

4. Real-World Results

By August 2025, @codexfx has achieved:

- $3 billion in annual stablecoin transaction volume.

- Projected $12 billion by September 2025.

- Deployment in the Philippines via partner PDAX for remittance transfers.

- Expansion into Indonesia, Singapore, Mexico, Brazil, Europe, and the UAE.

5. The Future: Stablecoins for Every Currency
@codexfx is expanding to non-USD stablecoins (VND, THB, IDR, etc.), helping to:

- Reduce USD dependency in regional payments.

- Increase liquidity for emerging market currencies.

- Lower costs for difficult payment corridors.

@codexfx is more than just another blockchain – it is the global payment infrastructure built from the ground up for the stablecoin era, fundamentally solving the problems of cost, speed, and transparency in international money transfers.

#CodexChristmas

Members of the Health Alliance for Democracy hold a protest at the Department of Health in Manila on Monday, December 15, calling for the resignation of Health Secretary Dr. Teodoro J. Herbosa.

The group accused Herbosa of failing to protect public health and alleged corruption within the Department of Health, which they said mirrors the controversy surrounding the DPWH.

📷: Mark Balmores | MB
